narrative: Material PL1__MD4FDBA6 shows stable, high-volume demand averaging 736.90 units/day with a moderate CV of 0.338, indicating predictable consumption with no significant trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.602), exhibiting a bimodal pattern between ~1 and ~3 working days, which is the primary driver of safety stock requirements. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: it fixes the order quantity at 4,274 units (constrained by storage capacity) and triggers replenishment when inventory falls to 2,432 units, achieving a 95% service level while respecting the 5,539.818-unit storage limit. The current SAP configuration of zero safety stock is inadequate given lead-time volatility.
warnings: Storage utilisation at 99.99% — order quantity capped from unconstrained EOQ 5,956 to 4,274 by capacity constraint
SAP safety stock is 0; stockout risk is high without implementation of recommended safety stock
Lead time CV=0.602 classified as UNSTABLE — transport variability is dominant risk factor

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Stable high-volume demand with well-defined mean and standard deviation makes EOQ-based (r,Q) the cost-minimising choice. Continuous review is appropriate given the high daily throughput and the need to respond quickly to the unstable lead-time environment.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds: unconstrained EOQ of 5,956 units exceeds capacity; order quantity reduced to 4,274 units. This increases ordering frequency (from ~4 to ~6 days), raising annual ordering costs by ~39% vs unconstrained optimum. Service level target remains achievable within the cap.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Storage utilisation is 99.99% of max_storage_units. Any increase in safety stock or demand surge risks physical overflow. Capacity expansion or lead-time SLA enforcement with supplier is strongly recommended to restore operational flexibility.
